title: Guadalupe (1531)
hookLine: Catholics tell of Mary appearing to Juan Diego, an indigenous man, near Mexico City

cards: A man takes the long way around a hill on purpose. His uncle is dying, he's running for a priest, and he doesn't want to be stopped.

On this hill, the story goes, a lady has been speaking to him, sending him with messages to the bishop, and he has failed to bring back the sign the bishop wants. He's embarrassed and he's in a hurry. So he goes around.
And she comes down the hill and meets him on the other path anyway.

teach.b: This is the story Catholics tell of Our Lady of Guadalupe, told in one old account in Nahuatl, Juan Diego's own language. Juan Diego is an indigenous convert living in the years just after the Spanish conquest of Mexico.
On the hill of Tepeyac, near what is now Mexico City, a lady appears to him, speaks to him in his own language, and asks that a church be built there. He goes to the bishop.
The bishop, cautious, asks for a sign. Then comes the uncle's illness, the detour, and the meeting on the other path. What she says there has become our line.
In the story, she tells him not to be troubled or afraid, and asks: am I not here, I who am your mother? Are you not in my care? She tells him his uncle is already healed.
Then she sends him up the hill to gather flowers, in a season when nothing should be blooming.
He carries roses down in his cloak, his tilma, and opens it before the bishop.

The roses tumble out, and on the cloth, the story says, is her image: a young woman with dark skin, in a mantle of stars, standing on the moon. Notice who the story honors. Not the bishop, not the conquerors.
An indigenous man the powerful didn't believe. It sounds like Mary's own song in Luke: "He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree."
The cloak hangs today in her basilica in Mexico City, and the Catholic Church honors Juan Diego as a saint. This is a Catholic devotion.
Other Christians honor Mary in different ways, and some don't accept apparitions at all.

how: Catholics in Mexico and beyond keep the feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe with processions, songs and Mass, and pilgrims visit her basilica at Tepeyac to see the tilma.

in the story, the bishop believed Juan Diego right away
he was cautious and asked for a sign; the roses and the image on the tilma became that sign.

games.q: you're Juan Diego. your uncle is dying, and you've failed to bring the bishop his sign. the lady's hill is on your way. what do you do?
o: go straight up the hill to her.
games.why: he went around the hill to avoid her, and the story says she came down and met him on the other path anyway.

practice: Remember someone with little power or money whose word you, or others, didn't take seriously at first: a child, a stranger, a worker, an elder. Hold what they actually said, and give it its full weight now.
If you pray, you can pray for them, or with Mary's words from Luke, he hath put down the mighty from their seats.

wordCard.voice: Guadalupe. Our Lady of Guadalupe, Mary as Catholics tell of her appearing to Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac, leaving her image on his cloak.

carryVoice: Your line: am I not here? Spoken to a man no one believed. That's nine hundred five.
